history.content: what makes the different shapes of the moon

The different shapes of the Moon, also known as lunar phases, are determined by the amount of sunlight that is illuminating the portion of the Moon visible from Earth. This changes as the Moon orbits the Earth and the relative positions of the Moon, Earth, and Sun shift. When the Sun, Earth, and Moon are aligned, with the Sun and Moon on opposite sides of the Earth, we see a full moon. When the Moon is positioned between the Earth and the Sun, we see a new moon. The crescent and gibbous shapes occur during the intervals between these principal phases, when only a portion of the Moon's surface is illuminated. The specific shape at any given time depends on the Moon's position in its orbit. When a sphere is illuminated on one hemisphere and viewed from a different angle , the portion of the illuminated area that is visible will have a two - dimensional shape defined by the intersection of an ellipse and circle ( where the major axis of the ellipse coincides with a diameter of the circle ) . If the half - ellipse is convex with respect to the half - circle , then the shape will be gibbous ( bulging outwards ) whereas if the half - ellipse is concave with respect to the half - circle , then the shape will be a crescent .

The average distance from the Moon to the Earth is about 238,856 miles or 384,402 kilometers. But this distance varies throughout the Moon's orbit, ranging from about 221,500 miles or 385,000 kilometers at its closest, to about 252,700 miles or 406,700 kilometers at its farthest resulting in a differential range of 50,200 kilometers or 31,200 miles. Lunar distance (astronomy) Astronomers O'Keefe and Anderson calculated the lunar distance by observing 4 occultations from 9 locations in 1952 . They calculated a mean distance of 7008384407600000000 ♠ 384 407. 6 ± 4.7 km , however the value was refined by in 1962 by Irene Fischer , who incorporated updated geodetic data to produce a value of 7008384403700000000 ♠ 384 403. 7 ± 2 km .

Storm drains may discharge into man - made excavations known as recharge basins or retention ponds .
What is a catchbasin and how they are designed?

A catchbasin is a component in a storm drain system that serves as a first-line pretreatment for other treatment practices. It functions similarly to the trap in household wastewater plumbing by capturing large sediments and street litter from urban runoff before it enters the storm drainage pipes. It is designed with a single large exit at its point of discharge, often covered by a grating, and lies immediately below the outlet of the storm drain. Water from the top of the catchbasin reservoir overflows into the sewer proper, and most catchbasins are connected to a piping system that leads to a canal, river, lake, reservoir, sea, or ocean.  Unlike the plumbing trap , the catchbasin does not necessarily prevent sewer gases such as hydrogen sulfide and methane from escaping. Its performance at removing sediment and other pollutants depends on the design of the catchbasin ( for example , the size of the sump ) , and on routine maintenance to retain the storage available in the sump to capture sediment . Some  catch basins are also commonly designed with a sump area below the outlet pipe level which is a reservoir for water and debris to help prevent the pipe from clogging

history.content: what is the defense of marriage act 1996

The Defense of Marriage Act (DOMA) is a United States federal law that defines and protects the institution of marriage. enacted in 1996. It was introduced by Georgia Representative Bob Barr and Senator Don Nickles of Oklahoma. The Act was intended by Congress to reflect and honor a collective moral judgment and to express moral disapproval of homosexuality. It also defined marriage for federal purposes as the legal union of a man and a woman as husband and wife, and a spouse as a husband or wife of the opposite sex. Section 3 of DOMA defines marriage and spouse for federal purposes. Section 3 codified non-recognition of same - sex marriages for all federal purposes, including insurance benefits for government employees, social security survivors ' benefits, immigration, bankruptcy, and the filing of joint tax returns, as well as excluding same - sex spouses from the scope of laws protecting families of federal officers, laws evaluating financial aid eligibility, and federal ethics laws applicable to opposite - sex spouses.

How are weddings celebrated?

The typical wedding involves a couple proclaiming their commitment to one another in front of their close relatives and friends , often presided over by a religious figure such as a minister , priest , or rabbi , depending upon the faith of the couple . In traditional Christian ceremonies , the bride 's father will `` give away '' ( hand off ) the bride to the groom . Secular weddings are also common , often presided over by a judge , Justice of the Peace , or other municipal official . At a wedding reception , the father of the bride , in his role as host , regularly offers the first toast , thanking the guests for attending , offering tasteful remembrances of the bride 's childhood , and wishing the newlyweds a happy life together . The best man usually proposes a toast in the form of best wishes and congratulations to the newlyweds . A best man 's toast takes the form of a short speech ( 3 -- 5 minutes ) that combines a mixture of humor and sincerity . The actual `` toast '' is then delivered at the end of the speech and is a short phrase wishing the newlyweds a happy , healthy , loving life together . The maid of honor may follow suit , appropriately tailoring her comments to the bride . The groom may offer the final toast , thanking the bride 's parents for hosting the wedding , the wedding party for their participation , and finally dedicating the toast to the bridesmaids .

What is the meaning of the glass being broken at a Jewish wedding?

The primary reason is that joy must always be tempered . This is based on two accounts in the Talmud of rabbis who , upon seeing that their son 's wedding celebration was getting out of hand , broke a vessel -- in the second case a glass -- to calm things down . Another explanation is that it is a reminder that despite the joy , Jews still mourn the destruction of the Temple in Jerusalem .

How many film adaptations of Hamlet are there?

I do not have specific information about the exact number of film adaptations of Hamlet. However, the earliest screen success recorded for Hamlet was Sara Bernhardt's 5-minute film of the fencing scene, which was produced in 1900. The film was an early attempt at combining sound and film , music and words were recorded on phonograph records , to be played along with the film . Seven silent versions were released from 1907-1921. Laurence Olivier adapted, produced, directed and starred in his screen version in 1948. Tony Richardson directed  the first Hamlet film in color in 1969. Franco A version by Franco Zeffirelli, with Mel Gibson and Glenn Close came out in 1990, and Kenneth Branagh's version was released in 1996. A version set in contemporary Manhattan and starring Ethan Hawke dates back to 2000. There have also been several films that transposed the general storyline of Hamlet or elements thereof to other settings . Yes, IBM Cloudant can store any JSON object subject to some caveats listed below
1. All documents must have two fields:
    * A unique _id field. The _id field is detailed in the next section.
    * A _rev field. The _rev field is a revision identifier, and is essential to the IBM Cloudant replication protocol.
2. Field names that begin with the underscore character (_) are reserved in IBM Cloudant. This rule means that you can't normally have your own field names that begin with an underscore. history.content: What are the steps to be taken to gather the relevant worker node data?

There are general steps to gather the relevant worker node data: First,  Check the conditions of your worker nodes and cluster before you gather data. This includes checking the CPU and memory level of your nodes. If any node is over 80% in either CPU or memory usage, consider provisioning more nodes or reducing your workload.Secondly if all worker nodes in a cluster, or in a single zone, subnet, or VLAN are affected, you can open an initial support ticket without gathering data. However, you might later be asked to gather the relevant data. If only one or some of your worker nodes are affected, you must gather the relevant data to include in your support ticket.  Before opening a support ticket, it is recommended to review the information and follow any troubleshooting steps in Debugging worker nodes, Worker node states, and Troubleshooting worker nodes in Critical or NotReady state. To gather worker node data, you can use the command 'kubectl top node' (for Kubernetes clusters) or 'oc top node' (for OpenShift clusters), which will display the CPU and memory usage of each node and once you have gathered this information, include it in your support ticket when you open one.

How can i update a classic worker node?

An update is available for your worker nodes in a classic infrastructure cluster. As security updates and patches are put in place for the API server and other master components, you must be sure that the worker nodes remain in sync. You can make two types of updates: updating only the patch version, or updating the major.minor version with the patch version. For Classic clusters with a storage solution such as OpenShift Data Foundation you must cordon, drain, and replace each worker node sequentially. If you deployed OpenShift Data Foundation to a subset of worker nodes in your cluster, then after you replace the worker node, you must then edit the ocscluster resource to include the new worker node.You can update the master Kubernetes version with the ibmcloud ks cluster master updatecommand. Remember that your worker nodes can be only up to two versions behind the master version (n-2). The worker node IP address remains the same after the update operation.

history.content: I cannot get select query to work, what steps should I take?

1. Check if you have the correct access rights: You need at least 'Reader' access to the buckets that contain the input objects. 2. After the FROM keyword, specify one or more unique resource identifiers (URIs) which can be thought of as tables. Each URI can specify one or more input objects, which can also be thought of as table partitions. 3. If the format of the input objects is CSV, and no special options are required, it is not necessary to specify a STORED AS clause. However, if the format is JSON, ORC, Parquet, or AVRO, after the FROM clause, specify STORED AS JSON, STORED AS ORC, STORED AS PARQUET, or STORED AS AVRO. 4. If text formats, such as JSON and CSV, are compressed with either gzip or bzip2 and have the extensions .gz and .bz, they automatically get recognized as compressed files. However, do not use these kinds of compressed files due to performance reasons. 5. If the format of the input objects is CSV and a delimiter other than the default , (comma) is used, you must specify the delimiter by using the FIELDS TERMINATED BY option of the STORED AS clause. All single Unicode characters are allowed as delimiters. 6. Check for a header line: By default, it is assumed that CSV input objects have a header line that specifies the names of the input columns.

Here are the steps to create a schema and tables: To create a schema: 1. Go to Databases. 2. Select the database in which you want to create a schema. 3. Click Create schema. 4. Type a name for the schema. 5. Specify the retention time interval (in days) for the schema. 6. Click Create. To create a table: 1. Log in to IBM® watsonx.data console. 2. From the navigation menu, select Data manager. 3. Select the engine from the Engine menu. Catalogs that are associated with the selected engine are listed. 4. Click Create and select Create table. 5. history.content: How can I delete a key?

To delete a key using IBM Key Protect, you can follow these steps:
1. Log in to the IBM Cloud console.
2. Go to Menu > Resource List to view a list of your resources.
3. From your IBM Cloud resource list, select your provisioned instance of Key Protect.
4. On the application details page, use the Keys table to browse the keys in your service.
5. Click the ⋯ icon to open a list of options for the key that you want to delete.
Please note that when you delete a key, it is "soft deleted", meaning that the key and its associated data will be restorable up to 30 days after deletion. After 90 days, the key becomes eligible to be automatically purged, or hard deleted, and its associated data will be permanently removed from the Key Protect service.
Also, keep in mind that deleting a key will make any data encrypted by the key inaccessible. If the key is restored within the 30-day time frame, this can be reversed. However, after 30 days, key metadata, registrations, and policies are available for up to 90 days, at which point the key becomes eligible to be purged. Once a key is no longer restorable and has been purged, its associated data can no longer be accessed.

After 90 days, the key becomes eligible to be automatically purged, or hard deleted, and its associated data will be permanently removed from the Key Protect service.
Also, keep in mind that deleting a key will make any data encrypted by the key inaccessible. If the key is restored within the 30-day time frame, this can be reversed. However, after 30 days, key metadata, registrations, and policies are available for up to 90 days, at which point the key becomes eligible to be purged. Once a key is no longer restorable and has been purged, its associated data can no longer be accessed.
what happen when the first user authorizes a key for deletion?

When the first user authorizes a key for deletion, it remains in the Active state for seven days. During this time, all key operations are allowed on the key. To complete the deletion, another user with a Manager role can use the Key Protect GUI or API to delete the key at any point during those seven days. Once the key is deleted, it will be moved to the Destroyed state. However, because it is impossible to purge an active key, another user must delete the key before it can be purged.
The key and its associated data will be inaccessible 90 days after being deleted. When you delete a key, it is "soft deleted", meaning that the key and its associated data will be restorable up to 30 days after deletion. You are able to still retrieve associated data such as key metadata, registrations, and policies for up to 90 days. After 90 days, the key becomes eligible to be automatically purged, or hard deleted, and its associated data will be permanently removed from the Key Protect service.
What could happen if no action is taken by the second user and the 7-day period experies?

If no action is taken by the second user and the 7-day period expires, the key will remain in the Active state and will not be deleted and you must restart the dual authorization process to delete the key . All key operations will still be allowed on the key. The key and its associated data will continue to be accessible and will not be moved to the Destroyed state. No further action can be taken to delete the key until the first user authorizes deletion again.
In case, the server expired, Could I remove the entry from the resource list?

In case  the server expire, you indeed can remove  the entry from the resource list and also  wait for the target time to trigger deletion for you, or even manually trigger the deletion from the resource reclamations.If an expired server is restored, only the entry within the resource list is restored, not the server itself.Restoring servers that belong to paid plans
Servers that belong to a paid plans do not expire, and that's why they can be restored during the reclamation period. If a server is restored, the timeframe for which the server was within the resource reclamations is billed to your account. After the server is deleted, only metadata, which isn't considered to be personal data is kept for 6 months. Make sure you back up important data for future use because you can't recover data after the virtual server has been deleted.
Why could not I delete keys?

One of the reason you could not delete a key it is when you are using the the Hyper Protect Crypto Services user interface. The service was not able to delete key "<key_name>". Because the key is enabled with the dual authorization policy and you set the key for deletion, a second approver needs to continue with the key deletion operation. Note that you will not be able to delete the key if it is protecting a registered IBM Cloud resource that's non-erasable due to a retention policy.
What could happen if I force a deletion on a key?

If you force a deletion on a key won't succeed if the key is protecting a registered IBM Cloud resource that's non-erasable due to a retention policy, which is a Write Once Read Many (WORM) policy set on the your IBM Cloud resource. You can verify whether a key is associated with a non-erasable resource by checking the 'preventKeyDeletion" field in the registration details for the key. Then, you must contact an account owner to remove the retention policy on each registered IBM Cloud resource that is associated with the key before you can delete the key. However, You must use the force option to delete a root key that is registered with another cloud resource.
Registrations are associations between root keys and other cloud resources, such as Cloud Object Storage (COS) buckets or Cloud Databases deployments.
Cryptoshredding .

The Cryptoshredding Key Protect provides for a force delete of a key that is in use by IBM Cloud® services, including your Cloud Databases deployments. This action is called cryptoshredding.Note that Cryptoshredding is a destructive action. When the key is deleted, your data is unrecoverable even from a soft delete state.

history.content: What are the steps involved to delete the CIS instance?

To delete a CIS instance, you must first delete all global load balancers, pools, and health checks. Then, delete the associated domain (zone). Go to the Overview page and click the trash can icon next to the domain name located in the Service Details section to start the deletion process.
If you are moving your domain to a different provider, be sure to migrate your DNS records and other configuration information to the new provider before activating the domain there. Activating the domain before migrating from CIS can cause your domain to change to a "Moved" state.
You can visit the IBM Cloud Internet Services for more information on how to delete the CIS instance. Delete the CIS instance if you created it specifically for this tutorial.

No, before you switch the traffic for your domain to CIS, it's important to import or recreate your DNS records in CIS. There are three main types of clouds: public, private, and hybrid.
A public cloud consists of shared resources that provide access to a company's resources. It is hosted in a multi-tenant environment on a virtual server and can be accessed from anywhere.
A private cloud consists of resources that provide access to a company's resources. It is hosted on dedicated hardware, such as a bare metal server, either onsite at the company's office (or across offices) or by a cloud provider. A private cloud can be accessed from anywhere.
A hybrid cloud is a flexible solution that combines aspects of both public and private clouds. It is hosted both onsite at a company's office or across multiple offices, and by a cloud provider. This allows a hybrid cloud to be accessed from any location, making it an attractive option for many businesses.

I am unable to provide a comprehensive overview of the evolution of cloud computing security protocols over time, but I can inform you about specific security features and practices related to restoring volumes from backup snapshots in IBM Cloud VPC. These features include data inheritance, encryption, and cross-regional backup copies, all of which contribute to a more secure and resilient cloud computing environment. Backup snapshots can be utilized to restore volumes in a different region for business continuity or geographic expansion purposes. The restoration of volumes from backup snapshots can be performed through the UI, CLI, API, or Terraform. By using the backup service, you can regularly back up your volume data based on a schedule you set up, with the option to create backup snapshots as frequently as every hour.
What is Data Encryption?

Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) encrypt your data and can be created and managed by your service or an IBM Cloud service. In the context of IBM Cloud VPC, data encryption can be applied to block storage volumes using either IBM-managed encryption or customer-managed encryption. When restoring a volume from a backup snapshot, if the source volume used customer-managed encryption, the new volume will inherit that encryption with the original customer root key (CRK).
It is the same as data backup and disaster recovery, right?

No, data encryption is not the same as data backup and disaster recovery. Encryption uses a two-way function to transform data into a form that hides its original value but can be converted back to the original state. On the other hand, the disaster recovery kit is an off-site and protected repository that includes hardware, software, and system secure configurations, as well as one-time keys and the disaster recovery plan. Meanwhile, data encryption keys are specifically designed to encrypt your data.

This provides cloud security and the flexibility to scale as needed. With IBM Cloud® Virtual Private Cloud, you can create your own space within IBM Cloud®. A virtual private cloud (VPC) is a secure, isolated virtual network that blends the security of a private cloud with the scalability and accessibility of IBM's public cloud. The Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) ensures network isolation and security within the IBM Cloud. It can serve as a foundational unit that encompasses a business division (such as marketing, development, accounting) or a set of microservices managed by a DevSecOps team.
What are the different types of clouds?

There are three main types of clouds: public, private, and hybrid.
A public cloud consists of shared resources that provide access to a company's resources. It is hosted in a multi-tenant environment on a virtual server and can be accessed from anywhere.
A private cloud consists of resources that provide access to a company's resources. It is hosted on dedicated hardware, such as a bare metal server, either onsite at the company's office (or across offices) or by a cloud provider. A private cloud can be accessed from anywhere.
A hybrid cloud is a flexible solution that combines aspects of both public and private clouds. It is hosted both onsite at a company's office or across multiple offices, and by a cloud provider. This allows a hybrid cloud to be accessed from any location, making it an attractive option for many businesses.
Is it free?

The VPC infrastructure is not free. The pricing varies depending on the regional location and sustained usage. When you provision storage, you need to select the right storage type and class for your specific use case. The charges will depend on the type of storage, its location, and the specifications of the storage instance. For some storage solutions like file and block storage, you can choose between hourly and monthly rates.

history.content: What are the advantages and disadvantages of Immutable data Storage?

There are some potential advantages and disadvantages of Immutable Object Storage:  
Advantages:  
1. Data Integrity and Long-term Data Retention: Immutable Object Storage preserves electronic records and maintains data integrity. It ensures that data is stored in a WORM (Write-Once-Read-Many), no-erasable and non-rewritable manner, which can be beneficial for industries like Financial, Healthcare, and Media content archives where data integrity is crucial. 
 2. Compliance: Immutable Object Storage can help organizations comply with certain regulations like SEC Rule 17a-4(f), FINRA Rule 4511(c), and CFTC Rule 1.31(c)-(d) that govern electronic records storage and retention. When using immutable Object Storage, it is the client's responsibility to check for and ensure whether any of the feature capabilities that are discussed can be used to satisfy and comply with the key rules around electronic records storage and retention governed by the above-mentioned regulations.
Disadvantages:  
1. Limited Availability: Immutable Object Storage is available in certain regions only. Users outside these regions may not be able to use this feature. 
2. Pricing: It requires a Standard pricing plan, which could be a disadvantage for users looking for more affordable options.  
3. No High-speed Transfer: It isn't possible to use Aspera high-speed transfer with buckets with a retention policy. This could potentially slow down the data transfer process.  
4. Irreversible: Once permanent retention is enabled, it can't be reversed. Objects uploaded that use a permanent retention period cannot be deleted. This means users need to be sure about their need to permanently store objects. 
5. Legal Holds: The retention policy is enforced until the end of a retention period and the removal of any legal holds. This could potentially cause issues if there are legal disputes or investigations. Please note that the actual advantages and disadvantages may vary depending on the specific use case and requirements.

history.content: How can I update the cluster master?

To update the cluster master, you should follow these steps:
1. Check if your cluster is unsupported by reviewing the State field in the output of the `ibmcloud ks cluster ls` command or in the IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service console.
2. If your cluster is unsupported, you need to create a new cluster and deploy your apps to the new cluster. Then, you can delete the unsupported cluster.
3. Before updating to the latest version, make sure to update deprecated clusters to a supported version that is one or two behind the current version. For example, you can update to version 1.21 or 1.22 before updating to the latest version, 1.23.
4. If the worker nodes run a version two or more behind the master, update them to the same version as the master to avoid issues with your pods.
5. Finally, update the cluster using the instructions provided in the IBM Cloud documentation: <https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/containers?topic=containers-updateupdate>.
Keep in mind that updating a cluster to a new version may impact deployed apps, so it's essential to prepare accordingly.

The CIS Kubernetes Benchmark is a framework of specific steps to configure Kubernetes more securely and with standards that are commensurate to various industry regulations. It is published by the Center for Internet Security (CIS). When a new Kubernetes version is released, IBM engineers compare the default configuration of a cluster that runs that Kubernetes version against the benchmark and publishes the results in the IBM Cloud documentation. I want to secure the phone connection before the integration

To secure the phone connection before integration, you can go to the Advanced options tab in the phone integration settings and select one or both of the following options:
1. Force secure trunking: This option uses Secure Real-Time Transfer Protocol (SRTP) to secure the audio that is transmitted over the phone.
2. Enable SIP authentication: This option requires SIP digest authentication for all inbound traffic. When this option is selected, the SIP digest user name and password must be configured, and the SIP trunk being used to connect to Assistant must be configured to use only TLS. However, if you use Twilio as your SIP trunk provider, you cannot enable SIP authentication for outbound SIP trunks to Watson Assistant.
Additionally, to configure how your assistant interacts with a SIP trunk from an external provider, go to the SIP trunk tab in the phone integration settings and update the SIP trunking integration section. Here, you can list the headers that you want your assistant to use in the "SIP INVITE headers to extract" field.

history.content: How to read bond yield quotes? What do the time, coupon, price, yield, and time mean?

Bond yield quotes provide important information about a bond's yield, which is the annualized return on investment for the bond. Here's how to read bond yield quotes:
* Time: This refers to the time of the quote presented and indicates when the quote was generated.
* Coupon (coupon rate): This is the amount of interest paid on the bond each period, as specified on the coupon itself. It is usually expressed as a percentage of the bond's face value.
* Price: This is the normalised price of the bond, representing the price of taking a position of $100 worth of the principal in the bond. It is often expressed as a percentage of the bond's face value.
* Yield: This is the interest rate that you would receive by buying at the current price. It is the inverse of the price and represents the annualized return on investment for the bond.
To summarize, when reading bond yield quotes, the time refers to the quote's generation time, while the coupon, price, and yield provide information about the bond's interest payments, market value, and annualized return on investment, respectively.

Indeed you can't deduct the value of your time or services, including the  value of income lost while you work as an unpaid volunteer for a qualified organization. It would be impossible for the IRS to determine the value of your time and it would open the tax system to an enormous amount of fraud (think of being able to make up time spent or writing off time spent volunteering at a soup kitchen or any other charity). history.content: how does pre-market trading work?

Pre-market trading takes place before the regular trading hours (RTH) of the stock market. For example, pre-market hours are from 4:00 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time (ET) on the NASDAQ stock market. During pre-market hours, you can place limit orders, but you cannot place market orders due to lower liquidity. This is because the volume and liquidity are generally much lower during pre-market hours compared to RTH. If an unexpected world event occurs, the volume and liquidity might increase. It is important to note that not all brokers allow pre-market trading, and if they do, you might need to specify that you want your order to be executed during pre-market hours.

what are limit orders vs market orders?

A limit order is a type of order where you set a specific price at which you want to buy or sell a security. The order will only be executed if the market price reaches the price you set. On the other hand, a market order is an order to buy or sell a security immediately at the best available current market price. Market orders do not guarantee a specific price, and the final execution price may be different from the price quoted at the time of order entry.
The choice between limit orders and market orders depends on your trading goals and risk tolerance.

Creating a single global market would be quite complex and challenging for several reasons. First, each country has its own exchange, which is closely tied to its local currency. Exchanges primarily support transactions and settlements in their local currency, and securities are denominated in a single currency. Cross-currency translation would complicate the trading process, as it would require additional steps and considerations.
Furthermore, citizens and businesses in most countries are restricted to having bank accounts in local currency, making it difficult or impossible to open a domestic bank account in a foreign-denominated currency. A public company headquartered in a given country is more likely to do business with local citizenry and businesses in that currency, and thus look for investors from the same pool, which generally means listing in local currency on an exchange in that country.

what factors pay major impact on the credit score?

The five factors that have a major impact on your FICO credit score are:
1. Payment history: Late payments can negatively affect your score, while on-time payments can improve it.
2. Credit utilization: This refers to how much of your available credit you are currently using. Lower is better, but having 0% usage is not ideal either. Aiming for 10% or less is a good goal.
3. Credit history: This is based on the average age of all your accounts, including credit cards and loans. Older accounts are generally better for your score.
4. Credit mix: Having a diverse mix of credit types (e.g., credit cards, mortgages, auto loans) can positively impact your score.
5. New credit: Applying for new credit can result in a temporary decrease in your score due to the credit inquiries made during the application process. These inquiries remain on your report for two years.
It is important to note that errors and fraud can also impact your credit score, so regularly reviewing your credit reports from the three major credit bureaus (Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion) is recommended.

The FICO score is a type of credit score developed by the Fair Isaac Corporation. It is widely used by lenders to determine the creditworthiness of potential borrowers. Credit Karma, on the other hand, provides users with free access to their credit scores, which are typically based on the VantageScore model, developed by the three major credit bureaus (Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion). While FICO and VantageScore models have some similarities, they are not the same and may produce slightly different credit scores. Therefore, the credit score you see on Credit Karma might not be exactly the same as your FICO score. However, it can still provide you with a general idea of your credit standing.

history.content: Alternative means of salary for my employees

There are different ways to consider salary compensation besides the traditional gross salary. Total compensation includes salary and bonuses, as well as the cost or value of employer-paid healthcare, retirement, company cars, expense accounts, stock options, and other valuable goods or services. Additionally, the total employee cost is generally double the gross cash compensation (salary + bonuses) and includes employer-paid payroll taxes and practical costs like the cost of your computer, cubicle or office furniture, and the portion of utility costs that keep you well-lit, clean and comfortable. It's also important to consider the cost of living in the area where your employees live, as this can significantly impact the actual value of their salaries. For example, $100k in California may not go as far as $100k in other parts of the U.S. Finally, it's worth noting that salary pay does not directly translate to hourly wages, as salaried employees are compensated for a week of work, which may require more or less than 40 hours.

Yes. In many countries, employers are required to report their employee's salaries and withhold a portion for income tax, which is commonly known as "pay as you earn," "withholding taxes," or taxing "at the source." Your employer uses the W4 form in the USA to determine how much to withhold from your wages. If you leave everything at default, your salary is your only taxable income, and you only benefit from default deductions. Your employer will calculate your tax withholding based on this information. When you start a new job, your employer will typically ask you to fill out a tax form such as the W-4 Employee's Withholding Allowance Certificate so they can withhold the correct federal income tax from your wages. If your employer doesn't do this, you are responsible for calculating and filing your income taxes, especially if you are self-employed, an independent contractor, or paid under the table. If your employer is reputable, they will provide you with additional information, usually in February. You must file your taxes correctly before the IRS tax deadline, generally April 15th for most people. Do I have to worry about money in my bank account? Unless you have a significant amount in your bank savings account earning interest, you won't have to pay any sort of tax on money in your bank account. If you do earn enough taxable interest, the bank will send you the proper forms to file your taxes.

history.content: My friend wants to put my name down for a house he's buying. What risks would I be taking?

There are several risks you might be taking if your friend puts your name down for a house he's buying.  Firstly, if you are co-signing the mortgage, the risk is that you will owe the bank the principal amount of the mortgage if your friend is unable to pay. You could come out of it a lot poorer and with your credit rating wrecked. Secondly, if you are not on the deed of the house, you would not have any legal rights to the property. This means that your friend could sell the house without your consent and you would still be responsible for the mortgage.  Thirdly, if your friend's house is a second home, he may not qualify for mortgage assistance or relief, increasing the risk for you as a co-signer.    Lastly, anyone considering this approach to talk to a lawyer and be aware of the potential tax implications.

It is important to note that trading stocks involves significant risk, and it is not recommended to invest money that you are not prepared to lose. Pump-and-dump scams are indeed very real, but the scale of a single scam isn't anywhere near the type of heist you see in movies like Trading Places. Stock market is like poker: you don't take the same risks when it is fake money and thus you don't learn the same lessons from your mistakes. history.content: Following an investment guru a good idea?

Following an investment guru can be a good idea if you can afford the time and are looking for more in-depth, fun investment tips. However, it's crucial to understand what you're investing in, including the company's products, and to buy stock in good companies at good prices, considering factors like price to earnings, price to revenue, and price to book. Therefore, while following an investment guru can provide valuable insights, it's essential to conduct your own research and make informed decisions based on your understanding and investment goals. Blindly following other investors, including big investors or gurus, is not recommended, as their strategies may differ from yours. Instead, consider finding someone with similar goals to help guide your investment decisions.

history.content: What does a small claims court do

A small claims court is designed to provide a fair, quick, and inexpensive way for individuals to resolve disputes involving relatively small amounts of money. You must have asked the defendant to pay and the defendant has refused. You may not have a lawyer represent you. The judge will hear your case or the court will give parties an opportunity to meet with a mediator at the time of trial. The Small Claims Court has a monetary limit on the amount of money damages that can be claimed, usually up to $12,500 for "a natural person", with some exceptions.

The web extension for federal government websites often ends in .gov or .mil. To ensure the site is secure, look for the "https://" in the website's URL. This indicates that you are connected to the official website and any information you provide will be encrypted and transmitted securely.
How can I protect my personal information from identity theft

Here are some tips to protect your personal information from identity theft:
1. Do not respond to or click on any links within unsolicited emails or pop-up boxes. They can put your personal information in jeopardy.
2. Be cautious when using your debit card online. Consider using a credit card instead as they typically provide added protection against fraudulent charges.
3. Only download mobile applications from official app stores and check other users’ reviews, as well as the app’s privacy policies, before downloading.
4. Use a variety of strong and unique passwords for your online activities. Avoid using the same password for all your accounts.
5. Keep your financial documents and records in a secure place. Shred sensitive materials before disposing of them.
6. Secure your wireless network with a strong password and turn on Wireless Network Encryption if available.
7. Lock your computer when you are using it in a public or shared space.
8. Regularly update anti-virus protection software on your computer and keep your computer system and browser up to date.
9. Double-check mailings and always make sure that documents are not stuck together and that the recipient’s information is correct before sending any Personally Identifiable Information.
10. Avoid sending any sensitive information via email. If you must use email, consider purchasing encryption software.
11. Use social media responsibly and monitor your privacy settings.
12. Consider purchasing and using a reputable Virtual Private Network or VPN software to use while online using public networks.
For parents, it's important to start the conversation about online safety with your children, establish rules, monitor their playtime, and teach them about cell phone safety.

history.content: What size should the bin be for compost?
In Madison County, NY., the bin for composting should be at least 3x3x3 feet in size.
can you please explain the steps for composting at home?

Sure, I'd be happy to explain the steps for composting at home as outlined by Madison County, NY. Step 1: Pick Out A Bin - The bin should be at least 3x3x3 feet in size. The location can affect how fast your compost dries out or holds water. A closed bin is recommended to keep critters out. If you use a closed bin, add a shovel full of soil from the ground. Keep your bin somewhere convenient to use and access. Step 2: Gather Materials - Browns are higher in carbon, and greens are higher in nitrogen. The optimal ratio is 3 parts brown to 1 part green. Avoid feces from cats and dogs, invasive plants, weed seeds, oil, fats, plastics, or non-organic matter. Gather kitchen waste in a container by your sink. Step 3: Maintain - If you have an open bin, layer some small sticks and twigs at the bottom to help with air and drainage. Layer your browns and greens, imagining you're making a bowl for your greens to lay in the middle and then adding more browns on top. Keep your compost at 40-60% water content, like a wrung out sponge. Turning helps a pile break down faster and ensures oxygen is present. Step 4: Harvest and More! - You will know when your compost is done when it has an earthy smell and looks like rich dark soil. If you do not fully turn the pile, your finished compost will be at the bottom of the pile. If you're running out of browns, shredded newspaper, paper towel, and toilet paper rolls make good brown additions. For more resources, you can check out www.compost.css.cornell.edu, www.epa.gov/recycle/composting-home, and www.dec.ny.gov/

history.content: What size should the bin be for compost?
In Madison County, NY., the bin for composting should be at least 3x3x3 feet in size.
can you please explain the steps for composting at home?

Sure, I'd be happy to explain the steps for composting at home as outlined by Madison County, NY. Step 1: Pick Out A Bin - The bin should be at least 3x3x3 feet in size. The location can affect how fast your compost dries out or holds water. A closed bin is recommended to keep critters out. If you use a closed bin, add a shovel full of soil from the ground. Keep your bin somewhere convenient to use and access. Step 2: Gather Materials - Browns are higher in carbon, and greens are higher in nitrogen. The optimal ratio is 3 parts brown to 1 part green. Avoid feces from cats and dogs, invasive plants, weed seeds, oil, fats, plastics, or non-organic matter. Gather kitchen waste in a container by your sink. Step 3: Maintain - If you have an open bin, layer some small sticks and twigs at the bottom to help with air and drainage. Layer your browns and greens, imagining you're making a bowl for your greens to lay in the middle and then adding more browns on top. Keep your compost at 40-60% water content, like a wrung out sponge. Turning helps a pile break down faster and ensures oxygen is present. Step 4: Harvest and More! - You will know when your compost is done when it has an earthy smell and looks like rich dark soil. If you do not fully turn the pile, your finished compost will be at the bottom of the pile. If you're running out of browns, shredded newspaper, paper towel, and toilet paper rolls make good brown additions. The Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act was passed in California in 1995. Rent control cannot be applied to any newly built housing completed on or after February 1, 1995.
Is there a housing problem in California?

Yes. In recent years, California housing costs have risen rapidly, particularly in terms of home purchase prices. The monthly fees for a newly purchased home are now about $2,500 higher than they were just a few years ago. The annual income required to qualify for a typical home is around $235,000—more than twice the median household income of about $85,000. To qualify for a more affordable "bottom-tier" home, the annual income needed is over 50% higher than the median income. The California Housing Finance Agency (CHFA) originally offered a first-time home buyer program limited to low-income households, but due to few households in this income bracket being able to purchase homes, the program has been expanded to include moderate-income households. As of September 2000, home buyers in 22 counties had received funding from the state.

Who invented mathematics?

The earliest applications of mathematics and geometry in relation to logic and philosophy can be traced back to ancient Greeks such as Euclid, Plato, and Aristotle. Many other philosophers from ancient and medieval times also employed mathematical ideas and methods to support their philosophical claims. 
Hellenistic geometers like Archimedes (circa 287-212 BC), Apollonius of Perga (circa 262-circa 190 BC), and Euclid (circa 325-265 BC) made significant contributions, with Euclid’s "Elements" becoming the most important mathematics textbook until the 19th century.
Ancient Greek mathematics introduced many key developments in the field, including the foundational rules of geometry, the concept of formal mathematical proof, and advancements in number theory, mathematical analysis, and applied mathematics. They came close to establishing integral calculus as well. The discoveries of several Greek mathematicians, such as Pythagoras, Euclid, and Archimedes, continue to be integral to mathematical education today.

Ancient Greece was a civilization that lasted from the Greek Dark Ages, which spanned the 12th to the 9th centuries BC, to the end of antiquity around 600 AD. Following this period, the Early Middle Ages and the Byzantine era began. Approximately three centuries after the collapse of Mycenaean Greece during the Late Bronze Age, urban city-states, known as poleis, began to emerge in the 8th century BC. This marked the beginning of Archaic Greece and the colonization of the Mediterranean Basin.
The Classical Greece period followed, starting with the Greco-Persian Wars and enduring from the 5th to the 4th centuries BC. The historical period of ancient Greece is significant in world history, as it is the first era documented through proper historiography. In contrast, earlier periods of ancient history or proto-history are primarily understood through circumstantial evidence, such as annals, king lists, and practical inscriptions.
The civilization of ancient Greece has had a profound influence on language, politics, educational systems, philosophy, science, and the arts. It became the dominant cultural force of the Roman Empire, to the extent that it marginalized native Italic traditions.
Was it a homogeneous society?

No. The territory of Greece is mountainous, which led to the formation of many smaller regions in ancient Greece, each with its own dialect, cultural traits, and identity. Regionalism and conflicts between these regions were common. Cities were typically located in valleys between mountains or on coastal plains, each dominating a specific surrounding area. Ancient Greece consisted of several hundred relatively independent city-states, known as poleis. This situation was quite different from most contemporary societies at the time, which were generally organized either as tribes or as kingdoms that ruled over larger territories. The geography of Greece, significantly contributed to the fragmented nature of ancient Greek society.
What is the Hellenistic period?

The term "Hellenistic" is a modern concept from the 19th century, coined by Johann Gustav Droysen in his work "Geschichte des Hellenismus" to describe the period when Greek culture spread beyond Greece after Alexander the Great's conquests. 
During this time, the center of Greek literature shifted from Athens to Alexandria, while other rulers, like the Antigonids and Attalids, fostered cultural centers in Pella and Pergamon. The patronage from the Museum at Alexandria was crucial for preserving much ancient Greek literature.
The importance of Greece itself declined, with Alexandria and Antioch becoming the leading cultural hubs. The Hellenistic period spans from Alexander's death in 323 BC to the rise of the Roman Empire, signified by the Battle of Actium in 31 BC and the conquest of Ptolemaic Egypt the following year.
Is architecture one of their great legacies?

Yes. Ancient Greek architecture was created by the Greek-speaking people (Hellenic people) whose culture thrived on the Greek mainland, in the Peloponnese, the Aegean Islands, and in colonies across Anatolia and Italy from around 900 BC until the 1st century AD. The earliest surviving architectural works date back to approximately 600 BC. 
A significant aspect of ancient Greek architecture includes temples and other public buildings, many of which remain as ruins, while others are still substantially intact. The open-air theatre is another important architectural form that has endured throughout the Hellenic world, with the earliest examples dating from around 525 to 480 BC. 
Other notable structures still evident today include the processional gateway (propylon), the public square (agora) surrounded by a storied colonnade (stoa), the town council building (bouleuterion), public monuments, monumental tombs (mausolea), and stadiums. 
Ancient Greek architecture is stylistically divided into three "orders," first described by the Roman architectural writer Vitruvius. These orders are the Doric Order, the Ionic Order, and the Corinthian Order, with their names reflecting their regional origins within the Greek world. While the three orders are best recognized by their distinct capitals, they also govern the form, proportions, details, and relationships of the columns, entablature, pediment, and stylobate. Each of the different orders was applied to a wide range of buildings and monuments.

history.content: what led to the development of the blues?

The development of the blues is associated with the newly acquired freedom of the slaves. As former slaves became acculturated, their secular and religious music began to reflect their psychological, social, and economic changes, and was linked to the national ideological emphasis on the individual and the popularity of Booker T. Washington's teachings.  The style evolved over a long period and existed in approaching its modern form before the term blues was introduced and before the style was thoroughly documented. Ethnomusicologist Gerhard Kubik traces the roots of many of the elements that were to develop into the blues back to the African continent , the "cradle of the blues.' Many blues elements , such as the call-and-response format , can be traced back to the music of Africa . The use of melisma and a wavy , nasal intonation also suggests a connection between the music of West and Central Africa and the blues. The first appearance of the blues is not well defined and is often dated between 1870 and 1900 , a period that coincides with the emancipation of the slaves and the transition from slavery to sharecropping and small-scale agricultural production in the southern United States. One important early mention of something closely resembling the blues comes from 1901 , when an archaeologist in Mississippi described the songs of black workers which had lyrical themes and technical elements in common with the blues. The launch of the field of race music by record companies like Paramount Records and OKeh Records, which was mostly blues targeted at African American audiences, also contributed to the development of the blues.

history.content: The English Bill of Rights.

The English Bill of Rights is an Act of the Parliament of England from 1689 that sets out certain fundamental civil rights and clarifies who would be next to inherit the Crown. It is a restatement in statutory form of the Declaration of Rights presented by the Convention Parliament to William III and Mary II, inviting them to become joint sovereigns of England. The Bill of Rights limits the powers of the monarch. He sets out the rights of Parliament, including the requirement for regular parliaments, free elections, and freedom of speech in Parliament. It set out certain rights of individuals, including prohibiting cruel and unusual punishment. It reestablished the right of Protestants to have arms for their defense within the rule of law. Furthermore, the Bill of Rights described and condemned several misdeeds of James II of England.
What is the basis of the Rule of Law in the United Kingdom?

The rule of law in the United Kingdom is a long-standing principle that has guided the country's governance since the Magna Carta in 1215 and the Bill of Rights in 1689. In the 19th century, constitutional scholar and lawyer A.V. Dicey discussed the two foundational elements of the British constitution in his classic work, "Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution" (1885). These two pillars are the rule of law and parliamentary sovereignty.
Do they have a constitution?

The United Kingdom does not have a single, specific constitutional document. Instead, its constitution, often referred to as the British constitution, comprises a collection of laws and principles that shape the country's political framework. This constitution is sometimes described as unwritten or uncodified. 
The British constitution primarily derives from four sources: statute law (laws passed by the legislature), common law (laws established through court judgments), parliamentary conventions, and authoritative texts. Since the Glorious Revolution of 1688, the principle of parliamentary sovereignty has been the foundation of the British legislative constitution. This means that the statutes passed by Parliament are the supreme and final source of law in the UK. Consequently, Parliament can alter the constitution simply by enacting new laws through Acts of Parliament.
How does Parliament work?

Parliament in the United Kingdom is bicameral, consisting of two houses: the House of Commons and the House of Lords. The monarch formally constitutes a third element of Parliament. The House of Commons, unlike the House of Lords, is democratically elected and holds supremacy due to the Parliament Acts of 1911 and 1949. An Act of Parliament represents primary legislation, and Parliament has the authority to alter the British constitution by passing such Acts.
Parliamentary supremacy has two key meanings. The first is that Parliament (the legislature) can create or repeal any law. The second meaning implies that as long as Parliament has the authority to legislate on a given subject, the exercise of that power cannot be challenged or reviewed by the judiciary. This latter meaning aligns more closely with federal systems, where judicial review cannot assess the merits of Parliament's exercise of power.
Parliament is not politically sovereign. This means that if Parliament enacts unpopular or oppressive legislation, it may not be enforced in practice.

What is SAML?

SAML, or Security Assertion Markup Language, is an open standard used to exchange authentication and authorization data between a provider that asserts an identity and a provider that consumes the identity information. It's based in XML and is a well-established framework for authentication and authorization standards. The SAML protocol provides a bridge between App ID (service provider) and your identity provider. When the identity provider authenticates a user, it creates SAML tokens that contain information about the user such as how they authenticated, attributes that are associated with them, or authorization parameters.
What is an identity provider?

An identity provider (IdP) is responsible for creating and managing information about entities such as users, functional IDs, or applications. The provider verifies the identity of these entities using credentials like passwords. After authentication, the IdP sends the identity information back to App ID, which authorizes the user and grants access to your app. 
Identity providers enhance the security of mobile and web apps through authentication. The IdP parses the SAML request, authenticates the user, and generates a SAML response containing its assertions. It then redirects the user and this response back to App ID. 
If authentication is successful, App ID creates access and identity tokens that represent the user's authorization and authentication, returning them to the app. Conversely, if authentication fails, App ID sends an error code from the identity provider to the app. Ultimately, this process determines whether the user is granted access to the app or its protected resources.
Can I use my own custom identity provider?

Yes, you can use your own custom identity provider for authentication. This identity provider can follow any authentication mechanism that is not specifically supported by IBM Cloud® App ID, including proprietary or legacy options.

history.content: What is the difference between CDN and IBM Cloud's Object Storage?

CDN, or Content Delivery Network, is a distributed network of servers that deliver content to users based on their geographical location. It helps to speed up the delivery of web content, such as images, videos, and documents, by caching the content at various locations around the world. This reduces the distance between the user and the server hosting the content, resulting in faster load times.
On the other hand, IBM Cloud's Object Storage is a service that allows you to store, manage, and access unstructured data, such as photos, videos, and text files, in the cloud. It provides multiple geographic locations in various data centers to provide content, and can be configured with a CDN front end for additional caching services.
In summary, CDN is a network of servers that delivers content quickly by caching it in various locations, while IBM Cloud's Object Storage is a service for storing and managing unstructured data in the cloud, which can be configured with a CDN for caching.
They sound more alike than different. Do they act together as a redundancy system?

While both CDN and IBM Cloud's Object Storage can be used to deliver content to users, they do not necessarily act together as a redundancy system. CDN is primarily used to speed up content delivery by caching it in various locations, while IBM Cloud's Object Storage is a data storage service. However, IBM Cloud's Object Storage can be configured with a CDN front end to provide additional caching services, which can help improve content delivery speeds and availability. In this setup, the CDN would pull content from the Object Storage if it is not available in its cache or if it has expired; with multiple data centers across the world, the CDN will serve the cached content from the closest location for your users; running on a different domain than your main application, the browser will be able to load more contents in parallel - most browsers have a limit in the number of connections per hostname. Before you begin using CDN with IBM Cloud Object Storage (ICOS), you'll first need to store objects with public access in IBM Cloud Object Storage. So, while they have different primary functions, they can be used together to enhance content delivery and redundancy.

history.content: What is the significance of CIS's reverse proxy?

The significance of CIS's reverse proxy is that it can compress and decompress content, allowing it to convert between compressed and uncompressed formats independently of caching. This means that it can pull content from a customer's origin server via gzip and serve it to clients uncompressed, or vice versa. Additionally, CIS's reverse proxy can handle multiple types of compression, including gzip and brotli, and can also handle requests that may otherwise cause errors, such as those with the Accept-Encoding header, which is not respected and is removed.
How to Brotli compression

To enable Brotli compression in CIS, follow these steps:
1. Log in to your CIS account.
2. Choose the appropriate domain.
3. Click the Performance tab.
4. Click the Advanced tab.
5. Toggle the Brotli switch to On.
CIS returns gzip or brotli encoded responses to compatible clients and browsers for the following content-types:

text/html text/richtext text/plain text/css text/x-script text/x-component text/x-java-source text/x-markdown application/javascript application/x-javascript text/javascript text/js image/x-icon image/vnd.microsoft.icon application/x-perl application/x-httpd-cgi text/xml application/xml application/xml+rss application/vnd.api+json application/x-protobuf application/json multipart/bag multipart/mixed application/xhtml+xml font/ttf font/otf font/x-woff image/svg+xml application/vnd.ms-fontobject application/ttf
reverse proxy with webP

CIS's reverse proxy is capable of converting between compressed and uncompressed formats, including WebP. WebP is a modern image format providing superior lossless and lossy compression for images.  WebP conversion does not change the image URL, and the Content-Type HTTP header is used to tell the browser the original format of an image. To ensure WebP is not served from cache to a browser lacking WebP support, it's recommended to disable WebP at your origin web server when using image size optimization.
When image size optimization is active, it adds the following headers to image requests that are compressed:
* cf-bgj: imgq:85
* cf-polished: qual=85, origFmt=jpeg, origSize=95005
* cf-cache-status: HIT
The cf-bgj header confirms that CIS applied image size optimization and returns the image quality setting (imgq). The cf-polished header represents the image size optimization status and returns the image quality setting (qual) and original size (origSize). The cf-cache-status confirms that the image has been cached and image size optimization can be applied.

To set up network connectivity for your bare metal server, follow these steps:

2. Enter `sudo nmtui` at the `core@localhost` prompt.
3. Click `Edit a Connection`.

5. Select `Show`.
6. Enter your CIDR for Addresses.

8. Add DNS server information. For example, for a public interface, the values could be 8.8.8.8 and 4.4.4.4; for a private interface, they could be 10.0.80.11 and 10.0.80.12. Repeat these steps for each of the wired connections that you want to activate.
9. When you are finished, select OK, Quit.

The ignition file is used to attach your bare metal server as a host in your Satellite location. You must configure a separate ignition file for each bare metal host that you are attaching to the location. The ignition file configuration process involves downloading the host attach script for your location, getting the host name for your bare metal system, converting the host name to base64, and then adding the host name information to the ignition file.

The ignition file "sparks" or triggers the setup and customization process of the operating system when the server is first started.  It contains essential information such as the host name, network settings, and other configurations that the system needs to function properly within a specific environment or location. You must configure a separate ignition file for each bare metal host that you are attaching to the location.

history.content: How does pre-market trading work?

Pre-market trading takes place before the regular trading hours of the stock market, typically from 4:00 AM to 9:30 AM Eastern Standard Time (EST). During this time, actual buyers and sellers participate in the market and get their orders matched. However, not all brokers allow trading during pre-market hours, and those that do may only allow limit orders to be placed, rather than market orders. Some brokers also require traders to specify that they want their orders to be executed during pre-market hours. If a trader places a limit order while specifying that they want it to be executed during pre-market hours, the trade can be executed in real-time at the specified price.

history.content: Help required on estimating SSA benefit amounts

Estimating Social Security Administration (SSA) benefit amounts involves calculating the Primary Insurance Amount (PIA), which is based on your average indexed monthly earnings. The PIA formula is as follows:
* 90% of the first $791 of your average indexed monthly earnings
* Plus 32% of your average indexed monthly earnings over $791 and through $4,768
* Plus 15% of your average indexed monthly earnings over $4,768
To calculate your benefit amount in the future, you'll need to estimate your projected average indexed monthly earnings and make assumptions about future bend points.  Additionally, you'll need to project the Contribution and Benefit Base, which limits the earnings used to calculate contributions and benefits.
The PIA calculation assumes benefits are taken at the normal retirement age. To adjust benefits for another age, you'll need to calculate an early or late retirement factor. Your benefits will increase each year based on annual changes in the cost of living.

Yes, IRAs (Individual Retirement Accounts) are effective retirement tools as long as their rules remain unchanged. What is the difference between a traditional IRA and a Roth IRA?

Both types of retirement accounts offer tax benefits. A Traditional IRA allows you to invest pre-tax money, which grows tax-free. However, withdrawing the money is taxed as income based on the amount you take out for that calendar year. 
In contrast, a Roth IRA requires you to invest post-tax money, which also grows tax-free. When you make withdrawals in retirement from a Roth IRA, that money is tax-free.

history.content: What is the difference between civil court and criminal court?

In a criminal case, the government files a case in court to punish someone for committing a crime, and the defendant is presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. If the defendant is found guilty, he or she may face jail or prison. On the other hand, a civil case happens when one person, business, or agency sues another one because of a dispute between them, usually involving money. If someone loses a civil case, they may be ordered to pay the other side money or to give up property, but they will not go to jail just for losing the case. Additionally, in a criminal case, the government must prove the defendant's guilt "beyond a reasonable doubt," while in a civil case, the plaintiff must prove his or her case by a "preponderance of the evidence" (more than 50 percent).
